mainTopic: רות's six blessed descendants, the meaning of סריסים, and why no book was named after נחמיה.
overview: The גמרא explains that the six measures of barley בועז gave רות were a hint: six descendants would come from her, each blessed with six blessings. These are דוד, משיח, דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. A פסוק lists דוד's six praises, and רב reads them as לשון הרע that דואג spoke about דוד's Torah greatness, which made שאול jealous. משיח's blessings come from ישעיהו 11, and רבא learns that משיח 'smells and judges', a test that בר כוזיבא failed. The virtues of דניאל and his friends are explained, along with a מחלוקת about their tribe. רב and רבי חנינא then argue whether 'סריסים' means real eunuchs or that עבודה זרה lost its power in their days, and each view is tested against פסוקים. Finally, the גמרא asks why no book was named after נחמיה. One answer is that he took credit for himself, and the other is that he spoke badly of earlier leaders, even דניאל, who was greater than the נביאים חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.

steps.title: Maybe it means six full measures
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting six literal grains, the גמרא suggests בועז gave רות six סאה of barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means six סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing from the previous lines, the גמרא offers a new reading of the 'six barleys' בועז gave רות: six full סאה measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six single grains would be a stingy gift, so the גמרא tries reading the word as a large measure. This sets up the next question.

phrases.english: Rather, six se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about the six barleys in רות.

steps.title: A woman can't carry six measures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a woman would not normally carry such a heavy load.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it a woman's normal way to carry six סאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'six סאה' reading: that is far too heavy for a woman to carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each literal reading fails. Six grains is too little and six סאה is too much. This pushes the גמרא toward a non-literal reading.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: And is it the way of a woman
to carry six se'a?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דַּרְכָּהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה לִיטּוֹל שֵׁשׁ סְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Six סאה is an unrealistic load for a woman to carry.

steps.title: The six was a hint to six blessed descendants
steps.stepSummary: בועז hinted that six descendants of רות would each be blessed with six blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he hinted to her that six sons would come from her, each blessed with six blessings: דוד, משיח, דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the number six was a hint, not a real amount. Six great descendants would come from רות, each with six blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both literal readings failed, so the number becomes a message about the future. The גמרא lists the six descendants, and the next steps show the six blessings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section that follows, which shows the six blessings of each descendant.

phrases.english: Rather, he hinted to her,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'he hinted', is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: that six sons are destined
to come out from her
who would be blessed with six blessings each.
phrases.notes: With the extra שֵׁשׁ in square brackets, it reads 'six six blessings', meaning six blessings for each one.

phrases.english: And these are they:
David and Mashiach, Daniel,
Chananya, Mishael and Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves from a literal reading to a hint
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The six was a real measured amount
steps.terutzMaskana: The six hints at six descendants with six blessings each

steps.title: דוד's six blessings from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק describing דוד lists six praises, which are his six blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד: as it is written, 'One of the young men said: I have seen a son of ישי from בית לחם who knows how to play, a mighty warrior, a man of war, wise in speech, handsome, and ה׳ is with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows דוד's six blessings by quoting a פסוק that praises him in six ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six praises are: knows how to play, mighty warrior, man of war, wise in speech, handsome, and 'ה׳ is with him'. This supports the claim from step 3 for the first descendant.

phrases.english: David, as it is written:
"And one of the young men answered and said,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:18

phrases.english: Behold, I have seen a son of Yishai
the Bethlehemite, who knows how to play,
and a mighty warrior and a man of war,
and wise in speech and a handsome man,
and the Lord is with him, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first descendant listed in step 3.

steps.title: דואג's praise was really slander about Torah greatness
steps.stepSummary: רב says דואג spoke this פסוק as לשון הרע, and reads each praise as a sign of דוד's Torah skill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: דואג said this whole פסוק only as לשון הרע. 'Knows how to play': he knows how to ask. 'Mighty': he knows how to answer. 'Man of war': he knows how to debate in the battle of Torah. 'Handsome': he shows insight in הלכה. 'Wise in speech': he understands one thing from another. 'ה׳ is with him': the הלכה follows him everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: רב says the 'young man' in the פסוק was דואג, speaking to stir up שאול against דוד. He then reads every praise as a description of דוד's Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain praises (music, strength, war, looks) become Torah skills: asking, answering, debating, explaining, reasoning, and having the final ruling. Saying these things was meant to make שאול jealous, which is why it counts as לשון הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: To debate, to argue back and forth

steps.confusionAlert: The words sound like praise, yet רב calls them לשון הרע. The point is that the speaker's goal was to make שאול jealous.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This entire verse
Doeg did not say it
phrases.notes: רב is telling us that the 'one of the young men' in the פסוק was דואג.

phrases.english: except as malicious speech.
"Knows how to play": that he knows how to ask questions;
"Mighty": that he knows how to answer;
"A man of war": that he knows how to debate
in the battle of Torah;
"A handsome man": that he shows insight in halakha;
"And wise in speech": that he understands one matter from another;
"And the Lord is with him": that the halakha follows him
in every place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב כׇּל הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה לֹא אֲמָרוֹ דּוֹאֵג אֶלָּא בְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching about the same פסוק quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג spoke the פסוק to stir jealousy, and each praise refers to דוד's Torah greatness.

steps.title: שאול becomes jealous at 'ה׳ is with him'
steps.stepSummary: שאול compared each praise to his son יהונתן, until 'ה׳ is with him', a quality שאול himself lacked.
steps.simpleTranslation: To all of them, שאול said: my son יהונתן is like him. Once he said 'ה׳ is with him', something even שאול himself did not have, שאול was upset and became jealous of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how שאול reacted. He matched each praise with יהונתן, but the last praise hurt him and made him jealous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first five qualities were also found in יהונתן, so שאול was not bothered. 'The הלכה follows him everywhere' was something not even שאול had, and that is where the jealousy started.

phrases.english: To all of them he said to them:
phrases.notes: The speaker here is שאול, answering each praise.

phrases.english: My son Yonatan is like him.
Once he said to him, "And the Lord is with him,"
a thing that even in himself
was not present,
he was upset and became jealous of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוּלְּהוּ אֲמַר לְהוּ יְהוֹנָתָן בְּנִי כָּמוֹהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why דואג's words worked as לשון הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the praise 'the הלכה follows him' triggered שאול's jealousy, because שאול himself lacked it.

steps.title: Proof that שאול lacked this quality
steps.stepSummary: Two contrasting פסוקים: about שאול, 'wherever he turned, ירשיע'; about דוד, 'wherever he turns, he succeeds'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For about שאול it is written: 'Wherever he turned he would condemn', and about דוד it is written: 'Wherever he turns he succeeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings פסוקים to prove that שאול did not have the quality of 'ה׳ is with him', while דוד did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases are almost the same, but שאול's ends with ירשיע and דוד's with יצליח. This supports the claim in step 6: דוד's rulings succeeded and were accepted, and שאול's were not.
steps.whatToRemember: The six measures were a hint to six blessed descendants. דוד's six blessings were Torah skills. The last one, 'the הלכה follows him everywhere', is what made שאול jealous.

phrases.english: For regarding Shaul it is written:
"And wherever he turned, he would condemn,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 14:47. Here the גמרא uses it to show שאול's rulings did not win out the way דוד's did.

phrases.english: and regarding David it is written:
"And wherever he turns, he succeeds."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 6's claim that שאול lacked 'ה׳ is with him'.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה followed דוד but not שאול
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 14:47 compared with the phrase about דוד

steps.title: How do we know the speaker was דואג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the servant who praised דוד was דואג.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that it was דואג?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's claim from Step 5 that דואג was the one who said the praises of דוד. It asks how we know this. This line sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'one of the servants answered' and gives no name. רב's whole reading depends on the speaker being דואג, so the גמרא wants a textual source for that identity.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
דואג האדומי, a servant of שאול

phrases.english: From where do we know that it was Doeg?
phrases.notes: He means the unnamed servant in the פסוק who listed דוד's praises.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שאול/דוד contrast and goes back to back up רב's identification of the speaker.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the anonymous servant was דואג.

steps.title: The 'one' servant is the outstanding servant, דואג
steps.stepSummary: 'אֶחָד מֵהַנְּעָרִים' is read as 'the outstanding servant,' and another פסוק names דואג as the chief of שאול's servants.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'one of the servants answered,' meaning the most distinguished of the servants. Elsewhere it says a man of שאול's servants was there, his name was דואג האדומי, the chief of שאול's shepherds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'אֶחָד' (one) hints at 'מְיוּחָד' (outstanding). Another פסוק tells us that the outstanding servant of שאול was דואג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. First, the word אֶחָד is read as מְיוּחָד, an important servant and not just a random one. Second, the פסוק in שמואל א 21 calls דואג 'אַבִּיר הָרֹעִים', the chief of שאול's shepherds, so the outstanding servant must be him.

keyTerms.meaning: The most distinguished of the servants
It is written here... and it is written there (linking two פסוקים)

phrases.english: It is written here:
"And one of the servants answered"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:18, the פסוק listing דוד's praises.

phrases.english: meaning the most distinguished of the servants,
phrases.notes: A play on words: אֶחָד ('one') is read as מְיוּחָד ('special, outstanding').

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"And a man of the servants of Saul was there
phrases.notes: שמואל א 21:8

phrases.english: on that day, detained before the Lord,
and his name was Doeg the Edomite,
the chief of the shepherds that belonged to Saul."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אֶחָד means the outstanding servant, and the outstanding servant of שאול was דואג.

steps.title: משיח's six blessings
steps.stepSummary: Back to the list of רות's six descendants: משיח has six blessings, listed in ישעיהו 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: משיח, as it is written: 'The spirit of ה׳ shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and might, a spirit of knowledge and fear of ה׳.' And it is written: 'וַהֲרִיחוֹ in the fear of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list from Step 3 of רות's descendants who each got six blessings. After דוד, it now names משיח and shows his six blessings in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six blessings are wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of ה׳. The גמרא also quotes the next פסוק, 'וַהֲרִיחוֹ', because its unusual word will be explained in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The Messiah, a descendant of רות
An unusual word, related to רֵיחַ (smell); explained in the next steps

phrases.english: The Messiah, as it is written:
phrases.notes: He is the next of רות's six descendants who each got six blessings (from Step 3).

phrases.english: "And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 11:2

phrases.english: the spirit of wisdom and understanding,
the spirit of counsel and might,
the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord, etc."
And it is written: "And he shall be inspired with the fear of the Lord."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 11:3. The word וַהֲרִיחוֹ sounds like 'smell', and the next two steps explain it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about דואג and שאול, the גמרא goes back to the list of six blessed descendants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיח's six blessings are the six qualities of spirit listed in ישעיהו 11:2.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי: loaded like millstones
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי reads וַהֲרִיחוֹ as coming from רֵחַיִים (millstones): משיח is loaded with מצוות and suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: This teaches that ה׳ loaded him with מצוות and suffering like millstones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלכסנדרי explains the word וַהֲרִיחוֹ. He connects it to רֵחַיִים, heavy millstones, to say that משיח carries a heavy load of מצוות and suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation is a sound-alike reading: וַהֲרִיחוֹ is close to רֵחַיִים. So the word is not about pleasure or smell but about a heavy burden placed on משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: He loaded him (placed a burden on him)

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:
This teaches that He loaded him
phrases.notes: The word וַהֲרִיחוֹ teaches this.

phrases.english: with מצוות and suffering like millstones.
phrases.notes: A play on words: וַהֲרִיחוֹ sounds like רֵחַיִים, millstones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word וַהֲרִיחוֹ quoted in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וַהֲרִיחוֹ means משיח is burdened with מצוות and suffering, like heavy millstones.

steps.title: רבא: משיח smells and judges
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads וַהֲרִיחוֹ as smell: משיח will sense the truth and judge by it, not by what he sees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He smells and judges, as it is written: 'He will not judge by what his eyes see,' and 'He will judge the poor with righteousness and decide fairly for the humble of the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of וַהֲרִיחוֹ. He says משיח can 'smell' who is right and judge that way, and he supports this from the next פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, וַהֲרִיחוֹ comes from רֵיחַ, smell. The פסוק says משיח will not judge by what his eyes see, so he must have another way of knowing the truth: a deep sense that 'smells' it.

keyTerms.meaning: Smells and judges (senses the truth and rules by it)

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's reading becomes the test the חכמים use in the story of בר כוזיבא in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said: That he smells and judges,
phrases.notes: He reads וַהֲרִיחוֹ as coming from רֵיחַ, smell: משיח senses who is right.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And he shall not judge by what his eyes see,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 11:3

phrases.english: "And he shall judge the poor with righteousness,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 11:4

phrases.english: and decide fairly for the humble of the land."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different explanation of וַהֲרִיחוֹ after רבי אלכסנדרי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיח will judge by sensing the truth, not by what his eyes see or his ears hear.

steps.title: בר כוזיבא fails the משיח test
steps.stepSummary: בר כוזיבא ruled for two and a half years and claimed to be משיח. The חכמים tested whether he could 'smell and judge,' and when he could not, he was killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר כוזיבא ruled for two and a half years. He said to the חכמים: I am משיח. They said to him: About משיח it is written that he smells and judges; let us see if he smells and judges. Once they saw that he could not smell and judge, they killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about בר כוזיבא (better known as בר כוכבא), who claimed to be משיח. The חכמים used רבא's sign from Step 12 as a test, and he failed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story treats 'smelling and judging' as a real, testable sign of משיח. Because בר כוזיבא did not have it, his claim was shown to be false.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader known as בר כוכבא, who claimed to be משיח

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of וַהֲרִיחוֹ: רבי אלכסנדרי says משיח is burdened like millstones, and רבא says he smells and judges. רבא's sign was used to test בר כוזיבא, and his claim to be משיח failed.

phrases.english: Bar Koziva reigned
phrases.notes: This is the leader better known as בר כוכבא.

phrases.english: for two and a half years.
He said to the Rabbis: I am the Messiah.
They said to him: About the Messiah it is written
that he smells and judges;
let us see whether he smells and judges.
Once they saw that he did not smell and judge,
they killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר כּוֹזֵיבָא מְלַךְ תַּרְתֵּין שְׁנִין וּפַלְגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing רבא's sign of משיח being used as a real test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who cannot 'smell and judge' is not משיח, as the case of בר כוזיבא shows.

steps.title: The six virtues of דניאל and his three friends
steps.stepSummary: The last people on the list of רות's blessed descendants are דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. The פסוק in דניאל 1:4 lists their virtues.
steps.simpleTranslation: דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, about whom it is written: 'In whom there is no blemish at all, good-looking, skilled in all wisdom, knowing knowledge, understanding learning, with strength to stand in the king's palace, and to be taught the writing and language of the כשדים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through its list of רות's descendants with six blessings each. It now reaches דניאל and his three friends and brings the פסוק that describes them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the list covered משיח and his six blessings from ישעיהו 11. Now the source is a פסוק in דניאל that describes the four young men chosen for the king's service. The next steps explain some of the phrases in this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemish or flaw (the same word as מוּם)

phrases.english: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
as it is written about them:
"In whom there is no blemish at all,
phrases.notes: דניאל 1:4

phrases.english: and good-looking,
and skilled in all wisdom,
and knowing knowledge, and understanding learning,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲשֶׁר כֹּחַ בָּהֶם לַעֲמֹד בְּהֵיכַל הַמֶּלֶךְ
phrases.english: and who have the strength to stand in the king's palace,
and whom they could teach the writing and language of the Chaldeans."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בר כוזיבא story and goes back to the list of רות's six blessed descendants from step 3. דוד was covered in step 4 and משיח in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה were blessed with six virtues, listed in דניאל 1:4.
steps.raayaObject: That דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה had six blessings

steps.title: What does 'no blemish' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far the phrase 'no blemish at all' goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'in whom there is no blemish at all'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops on the first phrase of the פסוק and asks what it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about how far the word 'all' (כׇּל) goes. Is it only about obvious flaws, or about even the smallest mark?

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for the meaning of a phrase)

phrases.english: What is meant by "in whom there is no blemish at all"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first phrase of the פסוק quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How complete the 'no blemish' description is.

steps.title: Not even a tiny scratch
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא says they did not have even the small scratch left by bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: They did not have even a mark like the scratch of a bloodletting lancet.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא בר חנינא answers that 'no blemish at all' means no mark of any kind, not even the tiniest one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'at all' as meaning the smallest possible flaw is also included. A bloodletting scratch was a common, minor mark, and even that was not found on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the scratch made by a bloodletting tool

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
Even a mark like the scratch of a bloodletting lancet
was not found on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'No blemish at all' means not even a tiny bloodletting scratch.

steps.title: What strength was needed to stand in the palace?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of 'strength' the פסוק means when it speaks of standing in the king's palace.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'who have the strength to stand in the king's palace'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about another phrase in the פסוק. Standing in a palace does not sound hard, so what strength was needed? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing still is not normally a test of strength. So the גמרא expects the word כֹּחַ to point to some special inner strength.

phrases.english: What is meant by "and who have the strength
to stand in the king's palace"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וַאֲשֶׁר כֹּחַ בָּהֶם לַעֲמֹד בְּהֵיכַל הַמֶּלֶךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a second phrase from the פסוק of step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of strength the פסוק is talking about.

steps.title: They held themselves back out of fear of the king
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that they forced themselves not to laugh, chat or sleep, and held in their bodily needs, out of fear of the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: This teaches that they forced themselves to hold back from laughing, from chatting and from sleeping, and they held themselves in when they needed to relieve themselves, because of their fear of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that the 'strength' was self-control. In the king's presence they held back every natural urge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strength in the פסוק is not muscle. It is the discipline to stay fully proper before the king for long stretches of time. Laughing, talking, sleeping and even bodily needs were all held back out of awe of the kingdom.

keyTerms.meaning: Their body openings, meaning their need to relieve themselves
Fear of the kingdom or the king

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
This teaches that they would force themselves to hold back

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַשְּׂחוֹק, וּמִן הַשִּׂיחָה, וּמִן הַשֵּׁינָה,
phrases.english: from laughing, and from chatting, and from sleeping,
and they would hold themselves in
when they needed to relieve themselves,
because of their fear of the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'strength' was the self-control to hold back laughing, talking, sleeping and bodily needs in the king's presence.

steps.title: Were all four from שבט יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the four were 'of the children of יהודה.' רבי אליעזר takes this literally: all four were from שבט יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Among them, of the children of יהודה, were דניאל, חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.' רבי אליעזר said: All of them were from שבט יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק about the four and asks which tribe they came from. רבי אליעזר gives the first view: all four were from יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads 'of the children of יהודה' as describing all four names that follow. This sets up a different reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of the tribe of Yehudah

phrases.english: "And among them were, of the children of Judah,
phrases.notes: דניאל 1:6

phrases.english: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah."
Rabbi Eliezer said:
All of them are from the children of Judah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the virtues of the four to the question of which tribe they came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, all four were from שבט יהודה.

steps.title: Only דניאל was from יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני argues that only דניאל was from יהודה, and the other three came from other tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: דניאל was from שבט יהודה, while חנניה, מישאל and עזריה were from other tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני disagrees with רבי אליעזר and says only דניאל was from יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'of the children of יהודה' as going only with the first name, דניאל. The other three are named alongside him but came from other tribes. So the same פסוק is read in two different ways.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת about the four: רבי אליעזר says all were from יהודה, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני says only דניאל was.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
Daniel was from the children of Judah,
while Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were from the other tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only דניאל was from יהודה; חנניה, מישאל and עזריה were from other tribes.

steps.title: What does 'סריסים' mean in ישעיהו's prophecy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes ישעיהו's prophecy that חזקיהו's descendants would become סריסים in the Babylonian palace, and asks what סריסים means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And of your sons who will come from you, whom you will father, they will be taken, and they will be סריסים in the palace of the king of Babylon.' What does סריסים mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from ישעיהו about descendants serving in the Babylonian palace and asks about the word סריסים. This sets up a מחלוקת in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of סָרִיס is a eunuch, but the word can also mean a royal officer. The question is whether the פסוק means it literally or in some other way.

phrases.english: "And of your sons who will come from you,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 39:7, said to חזקיהו. The גמרא is reading it as being about דניאל and his friends in the Babylonian palace.

phrases.english: whom you will father, they will be taken,
and they will be sarisim in the palace of the king of Babylon."
What does "sarisim" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new פסוק about the young men taken to the Babylonian palace and asks about one of its words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether סריסים in the פסוק is meant literally or in a different sense.

steps.title: רב: literally eunuchs
steps.stepSummary: רב says סריסים means real eunuchs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Actual eunuchs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the word means just what it says: they were made into eunuchs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב keeps the plain meaning of the word. According to him, the young men taken to the palace were physically made into eunuchs.

phrases.english: Rav said: Actual eunuchs,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 21.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: idol worship was 'neutered' in their days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reads סריסים as a play on words: in their days עבודה זרה was made powerless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא said: It means that idol worship was made powerless in their days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא disagrees with רב. He says the word is not about the men themselves but about idol worship losing its power in their time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links סָרִיסִים to נִסְתָּרְסָה, 'was neutered.' In the days of these young men, עבודה זרה was shown to have no real power. So the word becomes praise instead of a physical description.
steps.whatToRemember: רב reads סריסים literally as eunuchs; רבי חנינא reads it as a wordplay meaning עבודה זרה lost its power in their days.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא is not saying the young men were neutered. In his reading, the 'neutering' is about עבודה זרה, not the people.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:
That idol worship was neutered in their days.
phrases.notes: A play on words: סָרִיס sounds like נִסְתָּרְסָה, so idol worship lost its power.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing answer to רב's literal reading in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סריסים refers to עבודה זרה being made powerless in their days.

steps.title: How does רב explain 'they have no hurt'?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the three in the furnace had 'no hurt.' That fits רבי חנינא, but it seems to contradict רב, who says they were real eunuchs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says עבודה זרה was made powerless in their days, because the פסוק says 'they have no hurt.' But for the one who says they were real eunuchs, what does 'they have no hurt' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's view with a פסוק from ספר דניאל that says the three had no 'hurt' in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No hurt' sounds like their bodies were whole, with no blemish at all. That fits רבי חנינא perfectly. For רב, who says they were castrated, it looks like the פסוק says the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view), setting up a challenge to the other view

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says
that idol worship was made powerless in their days,
that is why it is written: 'And there is no hurt in them.'
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:25

phrases.english: But according to the one who says they were real eunuchs,
what does 'and there is no hurt in them' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁנִּסְתָּרְסָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בִּימֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views from steps 22-23 against a פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that they were real סריסים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק saying their bodies had 'no hurt' does not fit people who were castrated.

steps.title: No hurt from the fire
steps.stepSummary: For רב, 'no hurt' means the fire did not hurt them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means no hurt from the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב: the פסוק only means the furnace's fire did not damage them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is not talking about their bodies in general. It is talking about the furnace they were just thrown into, so it fits even if they were eunuchs.

phrases.english: Hurt from the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No hurt' meant their bodies had no blemish at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No hurt' only means the fire did not burn them.

steps.title: The fire is already mentioned in another פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק already says the fire did not touch them, so why say it twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is already written: 'nor had the smell of fire passed onto them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: a later פסוק already tells us the fire did not affect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'no hurt' only means 'not burned,' it seems to repeat what the later פסוק says. So maybe 'no hurt' is about something else after all, their bodies.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And the smell of fire had not passed onto them'?
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:27

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 25
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fire is already covered by another פסוק, so the first פסוק would add nothing.

steps.title: Neither hurt nor smell
steps.stepSummary: The two פסוקים teach two separate things: no damage from the fire, and not even its smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: Neither hurt nor smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two פסוקים are not repeating each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says the fire did not damage them. The other adds that it did not even leave a smell on them. So רב's reading holds.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב, 'no hurt' means the fire did not damage them, and 'no smell of fire' adds that it did not even leave a smell.

phrases.english: Neither hurt nor smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: One rules out damage and the other rules out even a smell.

steps.title: Would a פסוק call צדיקים by a shameful name?
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו calls them 'סריסים who keep My שבתות.' For רב, that would mean the פסוק names צדיקים by their blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says עבודה זרה was made powerless in their days, because it says: 'So says ה׳ to the סריסים who keep My שבתות.' But for the one who says they were real eunuchs, would the פסוק speak about צדיקים in a shameful way?
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to רב: a פסוק in ישעיהו calls these צדיקים 'סריסים.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנינא, 'סריסים' is a title of honor, because עבודה זרה was defeated through them. For רב it is a physical blemish, and it seems wrong for a פסוק to name צדיקים by their shame.

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says
that idol worship was made powerless in their days,
that is why it is written:
'So says the Lord to the eunuchs
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 56:4

phrases.english: who keep My Sabbaths, etc.'
But according to the one who says they were real eunuchs,
would the verse speak about the righteous in a shameful way?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁנִּסְתָּרְסָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בִּימֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב, using a different פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that they were real סריסים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק would not refer to צדיקים by a shameful physical blemish.

steps.title: Both meanings were true of them
steps.stepSummary: For רב, they were real eunuchs and also the ones in whose days עבודה זרה lost its power, so the name hints at the praise too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that were both true of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב: both meanings of 'סריסים' applied to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב can agree that the word also carries the praise that עבודה זרה was defeated in their days. So the פסוק is not only pointing to their blemish; it is also honoring them.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב, the three were real סריסים, and the word 'סריסים' also hints that עבודה זרה lost its power in their days.

phrases.english: This and that were both in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רב the word only means their blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב the word means both the blemish and the praise.

steps.title: 'Better than sons and daughters' seems to fit only רב
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק promises them a name 'better than sons and daughters.' That fits people who cannot have children, so it challenges רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says they were real eunuchs, because it says: 'In My house and in My walls, a memorial and a name better than sons and daughters.' But for the one who says עבודה זרה was made powerless in their days, what does 'better than sons and daughters' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the challenge goes the other way: a פסוק seems to fit רב and to be hard for רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comforting someone with 'better than children' makes sense if he cannot have children, as with a real eunuch. If they could have children, as רבי חנינא holds, why would they need this comfort?

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says they were real eunuchs,
that is why it is written: 'In My house and within My walls
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 56:5

phrases.english: a memorial and a name, better than sons and daughters.'
But according to the one who says
that idol worship was made powerless in their days,
what does 'better than sons and daughters' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from challenging רב to challenging רבי חנינא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's view that סריסים means עבודה זרה lost its power
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A promise 'better than children' only makes sense for people who cannot have children.

steps.title: Comfort for children who had died
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the comfort is for children they already had who died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Better than the children they already had, who died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא: the promise comforts them about children they had lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not have to mean they could never have children. They had children who died, and ה׳ promises them a name better than those children.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Better than children that they already had and who died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Better than children' means they could not have children.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means comfort for children they had who died.

steps.title: What is the everlasting name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'everlasting name that will not be cut off' in the same פסוק refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'I will give him an everlasting name that will not be cut off'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this promised 'everlasting name' actually is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about meaning, not an attack. The פסוק promises a lasting name, and the גמרא wants to know what concrete thing it points to.

phrases.english: What is 'I will give him an everlasting name
that will not be cut off'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the rest of the same פסוק

steps.title: ספר דניאל carries his name
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא taught that the everlasting name is ספר דניאל, which is called by his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said: בר קפרא taught in ציפורי: This is ספר דניאל, which is called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lasting name is the book of תנ״ך named after דניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A book of תנ״ך lasts forever, so a name on it is truly 'never cut off.' This also shows the פסוק is talking about דניאל himself.

keyTerms.meaning: ציפורי, a city in the Galil

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum said:
Bar Kappara taught in Tzippori:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה סֵפֶר דָּנִיֵּאל שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: This is the book of Daniel, which is called by his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The everlasting name is ספר דניאל.

steps.title: Why is no book named after נחמיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says all the words of ספר עזרא were said by נחמיה, so why wasn't a book called by his name?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, all the words of ספר עזרא were said by נחמיה בן חכליה. So why wasn't a book called by the name of נחמיה בן חכליה?
steps.whatsHappening: Since a book named after דניאל was just mentioned, the גמרא opens a new topic: why did נחמיה not get a book with his name?
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמיה wrote much of what is in ספר עזרא, yet the book was called by עזרא's name. The גמרא wants to know why נחמיה missed out on this honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all (opens a line of reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: Today there is a separate ספר נחמיה, but in the גמרא's time it was part of ספר עזרא. That is why the גמרא asks why no book carried his name.

phrases.english: Now, all the matters of the book of Ezra,
Nehemiah son of Hacaliah said them,
and as for Nehemiah son of Hacaliah,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אִיקְּרִי סִיפְרָא עַל שְׁמֵיהּ?
phrases.english: what is the reason a book was not called by his name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side topic that follows from ספר דניאל being named after דניאל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why no book was named for נחמיה

steps.title: נחמיה took credit for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says נחמיה lost this honor because he praised himself, asking ה׳ to remember him for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: Because he took credit for himself, as it says: 'Remember me, my God, for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: נחמיה pointed out his own good deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמיה asked ה׳ to remember the good he did, which sounds like self-praise. Because he gave himself credit, the book was not named after him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Because he took credit for himself,
as it is stated: 'Remember me, my God, for good.'
phrases.notes: נחמיה 13:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He praised himself, so he lost the honor of a book named after him.

steps.title: דוד also asked to be remembered
steps.stepSummary: דוד also said 'Remember me, ה׳,' so why is that not self-praise too?
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד also said: 'Remember me, ה׳, when You show favor to Your people; remember me with Your salvation'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: דוד said almost the same words, and nobody blames him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If asking 'remember me' is self-praise, then דוד did it too. So why should נחמיה be faulted for it?

keyTerms.meaning: Remember me, take note of me

phrases.english: David also said:
'Remember me, Lord, when You favor Your people;
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:4

phrases.english: remember me with Your salvation'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 35
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דוד used similar words, so they cannot be a fault.

steps.title: דוד was praying for mercy
steps.stepSummary: דוד was asking for mercy, while נחמיה was pointing to his own good deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד was asking for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that דוד's words were a request for mercy, not a claim of credit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד asked to be remembered as a gift from ה׳. נחמיה asked to be remembered 'for good,' meaning for the good he himself had done. The words sound alike, but the attitude is different.
steps.whatToRemember: נחמיה lost a book in his name because he pointed to his own merits. דוד's similar words were a prayer for mercy, so they are not a fault.

phrases.english: David was asking for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 36
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד and נחמיה said the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד asked for mercy, while נחמיה claimed credit for his good deeds.

steps.title: רב יוסף: נחמיה spoke badly of earlier leaders
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says נחמיה lost the honor because he spoke badly about the governors before him, and that included even דניאל, who was greater than he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says: It was because he spoke badly about the earlier leaders. The פסוק says: 'The earlier governors who were before me put heavy burdens on the people and took bread and wine from them, beyond forty shekels of silver.' And he even said this about דניאל, who was greater than him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second, different reason why נחמיה did not get a book called by his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה בר אבא blamed self-praise. רב יוסף blames something else: insulting the leaders who came before him. What makes it worse is that those leaders included דניאל, who was greater than נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: their shame or disgrace (speaking badly about them)
the earlier ones, the leaders who came before
'etc.': the rest of the פסוק continues

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that speaking badly about great people who came before you can cost you honor.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef says:
Because he spoke badly about the earlier ones,
as it is stated: "But the earlier governors who were before me
placed heavy burdens on the people
and took from them for bread and wine
beyond forty shekels of silver, etc."
phrases.notes: נחמיה 5:15

phrases.english: And even about Daniel,
who was greater than him, he spoke this way.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is counting דניאל among those 'earlier governors' נחמיה complained about.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסִּיפֵּר בִּגְנוּתָן שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 34, in place of רבי ירמיה בר אבא's answer (steps 35-37).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why was no book called by נחמיה's name?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because he spoke badly about the earlier leaders, even about דניאל, who was greater than him.

steps.title: How do we know דניאל was greater than נחמיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that דניאל was greater than נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that דניאל was greater than him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check one detail in רב יוסף's statement: the claim that דניאל was greater than נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's point gets its force from דניאל being greater, so the גמרא wants a source. This is a request for proof, not an attack on רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he was greater than him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a detail in step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that דניאל was greater than נחמיה.

steps.title: The פסוק: only דניאל saw the vision
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in דניאל: only דניאל saw the vision, while the men with him did not see it and ran away in fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And I, דניאל, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision. But a great trembling fell on them, and they ran away to hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a פסוק. This sets up the proof, which is finished in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that דניאל saw something the men with him could not. That alone does not yet prove much, because we still need to know who those men were.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְרָאִיתִי אֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל לְבַדִּי אֶת הַמַּרְאָה
phrases.english: As it is written: "And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ עִמִּי לֹא רָאוּ אֶת הַמַּרְאָה
phrases.english: and the men who were with me did not see the vision;
but a great trembling fell upon them,
and they fled to hide."
phrases.notes: דניאל 10:7

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְרָאִיתִי אֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל לְבַדִּי אֶת הַמַּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 39 by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק showing that דניאל saw a vision the men with him could not see.

steps.title: Who were the men with Daniel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats part of the פסוק and asks who the men with דניאל were.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the men who were with me did not see the vision.' Who were these men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats one part of the פסוק and asks who 'the men' were. This is needed to finish the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the פסוק proves anything depends on who those men were. If they were ordinary people, seeing more than them is no big deal. If they were great people, the proof is strong.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ עִמִּי לֹא רָאוּ אֶת הַמַּרְאָה״ –
phrases.english: "And the men who were with me did not see the vision":
And who were these men?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who the men in the פסוק of step 40 were, which is needed to finish the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the men who were with דניאל.

steps.title: The men were חגי, זכריה and מלאכי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה (some say רבי חייא בר אבא) says the men were the נביאים חגי, זכריה and מלאכי. So דניאל was greater than them, and certainly greater than נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה, and some say רבי חייא בר אבא, says: These were חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the men: they were three real נביאים. This finishes the proof that דניאל was greater than נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חגי, זכריה and מלאכי were נביאים, yet only דניאל saw the vision. So דניאל was greater even than נביאים, and certainly greater than נחמיה. That is why it was so wrong for נחמיה to speak badly about him.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: נחמיה lost the honor of a book with his name because he spoke badly about earlier leaders, even דניאל. דניאל was greater because he saw a vision that the נביאים חגי, זכריה and מלאכי did not see.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya says,
and some say it was Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba:
This is Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: זֶה חַגַּי, זְכַרְיָה, וּמַלְאָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 41 and so completes the proof asked for in step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The men were חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, so דניאל was greater than נביאים and certainly greater than נחמיה.
